mainTopic: צאן ברזל generations; a נדמה (look-alike animal) in בכורה, קרבנות, wool, and wine; and the משנה of twin firstborn males
overview: The amud opens by finishing the argument between רב הונא and רב יהודה about צאן ברזל taken from a גוי: how many generations of offspring are exempt from בכורה. Each אמורא rereads the wording of the משנה to fit his view, and the גמרא gives two versions (איכא דאמרי). Next the גמרא turns to a רחל that gave birth to an animal that looks like an עז. רב אושעיא brings a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר obligates such an animal and the חכמים exempt it. The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר obligates it in. It considers אותו ואת בנו and then settles on בכורה, explained through cases spanning several generations or, according to רב אשי, partial resemblance to the mother. רבי יוחנן adds that even רבי מאיר requires the שעיר of ראש חודש to be born from a goat, and the גמרא shows why both verses that exclude a נדמה are needed. A series of 'הכל מודים' statements then applies the rule 'just as linen is unchanged' to כלאים, תכלת, and נגעים. רב אשי extends the idea to wine from a vine trellised over a fig tree, and answers רבינא's challenge by pointing to a change in scent. Finally a new משנה begins about twin firstborn males whose heads emerge together, with the views of רבי יוסי הגלילי, the חכמים, רבי טרפון, and רבי עקיבא. The גמרא explains this משנה on the next amud.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words fit רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: According to רב יהודה, who holds that the תנא קמא extends the exemption past the first generation, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reply 'even until ten generations' makes good sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said to him: 'Even until ten generations they are exempt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a line that started on the previous amud ('it works well for רב יהודה'). It shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's wording supports רב יהודה's reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה holds that the תנא קמא already exempts more than one generation. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's word 'even' then means he goes further than the תנא קמא, all the way to ten generations. The word 'even' fits naturally only if the תנא קמא was also talking about generations.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who disagrees with the תנא קמא in this משנה
Even up to ten generations
Exempt (here, from the law of בכורה)
This is why he said; it shows a statement fits a view

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the second half of a 'בשלמא' (it works well for X) argument that began on the previous amud. The real point is the contrast that comes next: 'but according to רב הונא, what does it mean?'

phrases.english: This is what he said to him
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel:
Even until ten generations they are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'בשלמא לרב יהודה' half of the argument earlier
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's view that the תנא קמא exempts more than one generation
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's phrase 'even until ten generations' in the משנה

steps.title: What does 'even ten generations' mean for רב הונא?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds that the תנא קמא did not extend the exemption past the first generation. So what is the word 'even' adding?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב הונא, who says the תנא קמא did not go down into later generations, what is the meaning of 'even until ten generations'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. If the תנא קמא only exempts the first generation, then רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's word 'even' seems to have nothing to build on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Even' suggests that the other side already accepted some number of generations, and this opinion simply goes further. If the תנא קמא never spoke about multiple generations, the phrasing of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל looks strange.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes down into generations, i.e., extends the law to later generations
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה
What is the meaning of

phrases.english: But according to Rav Huna, who says:
the first tanna did not descend to generations,
what is 'even until ten generations'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The contrasting half of the בשלמא/אלא structure: it works for רב יהודה, but how does it work for רב הונא?
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's reading of the תנא קמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'even' implies that the תנא קמא also extended the exemption across generations, which contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: רב הונא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is responding to the 'העמיד' case
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is reacting to the משנה's second case, where the Jew 'established' the offspring in place of the mothers. In that case the תנא קמא does extend the exemption to a further generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא could tell you: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is referring to the case of 'he established', where the תנא קמא does go down into generations.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends himself. He says 'even' is aimed at a different clause of the משנה, the 'העמיד' case, where the תנא קמא also exempts more than one generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the העמיד case, the offspring replace the mothers, so the offspring of the offspring are also exempt even according to the תנא קמא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's 'even ten generations' builds on that clause, not the first one. So the first clause can still stop at one generation, as רב הונא says.

keyTerms.meaning: He established, i.e., set the offspring in place of the original mothers
Is standing on, i.e., is referring to
He could say to you; introduces a defense

phrases.english: Rav Huna could say to you:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
is referring to the case of 'he established'
where he does descend to generations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב הונא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the statement to a different clause of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Even' was thought to respond to the first clause, implying the תנא קמא exempts several generations there.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Even' responds to the העמיד clause, where the תנא קמא does go down a generation. In the first clause, רב הונא's single-generation reading stands.

steps.title: The משנה's wording seems to refute רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'offspring are exempt, offspring of offspring are not.' This appears to contradict רב יהודה, who exempts the offspring of offspring too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who receives צאן ברזל from a גוי: the offspring are exempt, and the offspring of the offspring are not. This is a refutation of רב יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the plain wording of the משנה to attack רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly says the second generation ('offspring of offspring') is not exempt. רב יהודה says that generation is exempt, so his view seems to contradict the words of the משנה directly.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; introduces a source used as proof or challenge
An 'iron flock' investment, where the owner's principal is guaranteed
The offspring of the offspring
A conclusive refutation

phrases.english: Come and hear:
one who accepts a guaranteed-investment flock from a gentile —
the offspring are exempt,
and the offspring of the offspring are not.
A refutation of Rav Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַמְקַבֵּל צֹאן בַּרְזֶל מִן הַגּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב הונא, the גמרא now challenges רב יהודה from the משנה's wording
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's view that the offspring of offspring are exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly says the offspring of offspring are 'not' exempt.

steps.title: רב יהודה rereads the משנה as 'they and their offspring'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reads 'offspring are exempt' as 'they (the direct offspring) and their offspring are exempt'. So two generations are included in the exemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה could tell you: Say it means 'they and their offspring.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה defends himself by reinterpreting the משנה's words so that the exemption covers two generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By reading 'offspring' as 'the offspring and their offspring', רב יהודה pushes the exemption one generation further. The 'not exempt' in the משנה then refers to the generation after that, so the משנה no longer contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: Say; read the text as follows
They and their offspring

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda could say to you: Say:
they and their offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation against רב יהודה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Offspring are exempt' means only the first generation.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Offspring' includes the direct offspring together with their offspring, which matches רב יהודה.

steps.title: Second version: the משנה seems to refute רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: According to another version, the משנה's text actually reads 'they and their offspring are exempt'. That wording seems to refute רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: the text reads 'they and their offspring are exempt.' This is a refutation of רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the exchange (איכא דאמרי). Here the משנה's wording itself is 'they and their offspring', and this becomes a challenge to רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה explicitly says 'they and their offspring', then two generations are exempt. That contradicts רב הונא, who exempts only one generation. This version flips who is under attack.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say; introduces an alternate version

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument added on top of the previous ones. It is a different version of the same exchange. In this version the משנה's text itself says 'they and their offspring', so now רב הונא needs to defend himself instead of רב יהודה.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
they and their offspring are exempt,
a refutation of Rav Huna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternate version of steps 4 and 5, with the attack aimed at רב הונא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that only the direct offspring are exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'they and their offspring' seems to exempt two generations.

steps.title: רב הונא: 'they' are the original animals
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reads 'they' as the original animals and 'their offspring' as the first generation, which is exempt. The offspring of the offspring remain obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא could tell you: Say 'they and the offspring' are exempt, but the offspring of the offspring are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends himself by explaining that 'they' means the original mother animals. So only one generation of offspring is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה took 'they' to mean the first offspring, which yields two exempt generations. רב הונא takes 'they' to mean the original animals given by the גוי. That shifts everything back one level, so the משנה matches his single-generation view.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt
Obligated (in בכורה)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the משנה's wording. In each one, only the אמורא who seems refuted rereads the text to fit his view. If the text reads 'offspring are exempt, offspring of offspring are not', רב יהודה reads it as 'they (the offspring) and their offspring', so two generations are exempt. If the text reads 'they and their offspring', רב הונא reads 'they' as the original animals, so only one generation of offspring is exempt.

phrases.english: Rav Huna could say to you:
say: they and the offspring — exempt,
and the offspring of the offspring — obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב הוּנָא: אֵימָא הֵן וְולָדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation against רב הונא in the second version
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'They' are the first offspring, so two generations are exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'They' are the original animals and only their direct offspring are exempt. The offspring of the offspring are obligated.

steps.title: New section: a ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה: a רחל that gave birth to an animal that looks like an עז.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ewe that gave birth to a kind of goat, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new topic in the משנה and quotes its opening words. This line sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that when a רחל gives birth to an animal that looks like an עז, it is exempt from בכורה. The verse requires the firstborn to be the same kind as its mother. Quoting these words marks the start of the גמרא's discussion of this case.

keyTerms.meaning: A ewe (female sheep)
A kind of goat; an animal with a goat's appearance
Etc.; the quote of the משנה continues

phrases.english: A ewe that gave birth to a kind of goat, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the צאן ברזל discussion and opens a new clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רחל that gives birth to an עז-like animal (and the reverse) is exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: רב אושעיא's ברייתא: רבי מאיר obligates, the חכמים exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא arrives from נהרדעא with a ברייתא. It records a dispute: רבי מאיר obligates a רחל born to an עז (or the reverse) in בכורה, and the חכמים exempt it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא came from נהרדעא and brought a ברייתא with him: A ewe born to a goat, or a goat born to a ewe: רבי מאיר obligates it, and the חכמים exempt it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new source is brought: a ברייתא showing that the משנה's exemption is actually a dispute. רבי מאיר disagrees and holds the animal is obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated the exemption without naming anyone. This ברייתא reveals that the exemption is the view of the חכמים, while רבי מאיר obligates. It sets up the coming discussion of why they disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who brought this ברייתא
נהרדעא, a major Torah center in Babylonia
A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה
Holds it obligated
Hold it exempt

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's seemingly simple exemption is the view of the חכמים against רבי מאיר. This becomes the base for the analysis that follows.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya came from Neharde'a,
and brought a baraita in his hand:

phrases.aramaic: רָחֵל בַּת עֵז, וְעֵז בַּת רָחֵל —
phrases.english: a ewe born to a goat, and a goat born to a ewe —
Rabbi Meir deems it obligated,
and the Rabbis deem it exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא וְאַיְיתִי מַתְנִיתָא בִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that adds a dispute to the משנה's clause
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a רחל born to an עז or an עז born to a רחל, רבי מאיר obligates it in בכורה and the חכמים exempt it.

steps.title: רב הושעיא asks what רבי מאיר obligates
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא tells רבה to ask רב הונא which obligation רבי מאיר means in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said to רבה: When you go in before רב הונא, ask him: What does רבי מאיר obligate it in?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the ברייתא from step 9: what does 'obligated' mean for רבי מאיר? This line sets up the next steps, which test the possible answers one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'רבי מאיר obligates' but never said in what. Now the גמרא wants to pin down which מצוה is meant. The next two steps rule out the obvious options.

keyTerms.meaning: When you go in
Ask him
Obligates in what?

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said to Rabba:
When you go in before Rav Huna,
ask him:
Rabbi Meir obligates it in what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the ruling in the ברייתא of step 9 actually refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which obligation (בכורה, ראשית הגז, or something else) רבי מאיר applies to a רחל born to an עז.

steps.title: It cannot mean the firstborn obligation
steps.stepSummary: If רבי מאיר means בכורה, he would contradict the פסוק 'אך בכור שור', which requires the firstborn to be the same kind as its mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he obligates it in בכורה: doesn't רבי מאיר accept 'אך בכור שור', which teaches that the law applies only when the mother is an ox and her firstborn is an ox?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible answer, בכורה, and rejects it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'אך בכור שור' is understood to require that the mother and the firstborn look like the same species. A sheep born looking like a goat fails that rule. So רבי מאיר could not obligate it in בכורה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say
The firstborn obligation
'But the firstborn of an ox' (במדבר יח:יז)
Doesn't he hold?

phrases.english: If you say it is the firstborn obligation —
doesn't Rabbi Meir hold
'But the firstborn of an ox'

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא שׁוֹר וּבְכוֹרוֹ שׁוֹר?
phrases.english: only when it is an ox and its firstborn is an ox?
phrases.notes: The offspring must match its mother's species.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rules out the first possible answer to the question in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that רבי מאיר means בכורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אך בכור שור' requires the mother and the offspring to be the same kind. A goat-like sheep is not, so it cannot be obligated in בכורה.

steps.title: It cannot mean the first-shearing obligation
steps.stepSummary: If רבי מאיר means ראשית הגז, he would contradict the teaching of דבי רבי ישמעאל that sheep with tough wool are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he obligates it in ראשית הגז. But doesn't he accept what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: sheep with tough wool are exempt from ראשית הגז, as it says, 'and he was warmed by the fleece of my sheep'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second answer, ראשית הגז, and rejects that too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in איוב shows that only wool soft enough to warm a person counts for ראשית הגז. A sheep that looks like a goat has tough, goat-like hair. So it should be exempt from ראשית הגז as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The first shearing of wool, given to a כהן
The school of רבי ישמעאל taught
Their wool is tough
He would be warmed (איוב לא:כ)

phrases.english: Rather, it is the first shearing of wool,
but doesn't he hold this
which the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Sheep whose wool is tough
are exempt from the first shearing,
as it says: 'And with the fleece of my sheep he was warmed'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting בכורה, tries ראשית הגז and rejects it too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that רבי מאיר means ראשית הגז
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tough wool is exempt according to דבי רבי ישמעאל. A goat-like sheep has tough hair, so it cannot be obligated.

steps.title: The dispute is about slaughtering an animal and its offspring when the father is a goat
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the case is a ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal whose father is a goat. The dispute is whether we consider the father's line for אותו ואת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Let us see what case we are dealing with. A ewe gave birth to a goat-like animal, and its father is a goat. They argue about whether we take the father into account for אותו ואת בנו. רבי מאיר holds we take the father into account, and the רבנן hold we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה offers a new reading: 'obligated' is about the איסור of slaughtering an animal and its offspring on the same day, not about בכורה or wool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father is a goat, and the offspring looks like a goat, so father and child match. רבי מאיר says a person who slaughters both on one day is חייב for אותו ואת בנו, because we consider the father's line. The חכמים say we only consider the mother, so he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
A male goat
We take the father's line into account
The איסור of slaughtering an animal and its offspring on the same day

steps.confusionAlert: 'Obligated' here does not mean obligated in a מצוה of giving. It means חייב (liable) for slaughtering the father and its offspring on the same day.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a word like 'חייב' in a ברייתא can refer to a completely different area of הלכה than the one the topic seems to suggest.

phrases.english: He said to him: Let us see,
what case are we dealing with here?
A ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal,
and its father is a male goat,
and they argue about whether we consider the father's line
for the law of an animal and its offspring,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְזֶרַע הָאָב,
phrases.english: since Rabbi Meir holds: we consider the father's line,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְזֶרַע הָאָב.
phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold: we do not consider the father's line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 after steps 11 and 12 ruled out בכורה and ראשית הגז.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the case (הכא במאי עסקינן) and moving the ruling to a different area of הלכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Obligated' refers to a מצוה of giving, either בכורה or ראשית הגז.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Obligated' refers to liability for אותו ואת בנו when the father is a goat. רבי מאיר considers the father's line and the רבנן do not.

steps.title: Then they should have argued about the father's line in general
steps.stepSummary: If the real dispute is about the father's line, the ברייתא should have stated that general dispute, the argument of חנניה and the רבנן, instead of this unusual case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let them argue about considering the father's line in general, as in the dispute of חנניה and the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's answer: why would the ברייתא choose such a strange case to show a general dispute?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether אותו ואת בנו applies to the father is already a known general argument between חנניה and the רבנן (חולין עח:). If that were the issue here, there would be no reason to bring a ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal. The odd case suggests the dispute must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
In general
The dispute of חנניה and the רבנן

phrases.english: If so,
let them argue about considering the father's line in general,
as in the dispute of Ḥananya and the Rabbis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's explanation that the dispute is about considering the father's line for אותו ואת בנו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general dispute should be taught in general terms. The ברייתא's specific, unusual case makes no sense if the issue is simply the father's line, which is already the known dispute of חנניה and the רבנן.

steps.title: Back to firstborn: a ewe born to a ewe that came from a goat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the father-line explanation. It says the ברייתא is about בכורה after all, in a case of a ewe born to a ewe whose own mother was a goat. רבי מאיר follows the mother, so the animal is not a נדמה. חכמים follow the grandmother, so the animal is a נדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא really is about בכורה. The case is a ewe born to a ewe, which was itself born to a goat. One master (רבי מאיר) holds that we follow the animal's mother, and this newborn looks like its mother, so it is not a 'look-alike'. The other master (חכמים) holds that we follow the mother's mother, and this newborn does not look like the goat grandmother, so it is a 'look-alike'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer: רבי מאיר really is talking about בכורה, and the case involves three generations, a goat, then a sheep, then a sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem in step 11 was that 'אך בכור שור' requires the firstborn to match its mother. Here the newborn does match its direct mother, so רבי מאיר does not contradict the פסוק. חכמים say the true identity comes from the grandmother (a goat), so this sheep counts as a נדמה and is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; it returns to an option that was set aside earlier
What case are we dealing with? It introduces a specific scenario
A ewe born to a ewe that was itself born to a goat
Go after its mother: the animal's status follows its direct mother
A 'look-alike': an animal that looks like a different species from its mother, which is exempt from בכורה

steps.confusionAlert: The newborn here is a sheep that looks like its sheep mother. The 'odd' part is one generation back, because its mother was born to a goat. Do not picture the newborn itself as looking like a goat.

phrases.english: Rather, it really refers to the firstborn obligation,
and here, what case are we dealing with?
With a ewe, daughter of a ewe, daughter of a goat.
phrases.notes: Three generations: goat, then sheep, then sheep (the newborn).

phrases.english: One master holds: follow its mother,
and this one is not a look-alike.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: זִיל בָּתַר אִימַּיהּ דְּאִימֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: And the other master holds: follow its mother's mother,
and this one is a look-alike.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְעוֹלָם לִבְכוֹרָה, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 14 by abandoning רבה's father-line case and returning to the בכורה reading with a new case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reading רבי מאיר as talking about בכורה seemed to clash with 'אך בכור שור'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The newborn matches its direct mother, so the פסוק is satisfied for רבי מאיר. The dispute is whether to look at the mother or the grandmother.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'matching the mother' can be defined by one generation or by two.

steps.title: Second option: a ewe born to a goat that came from a ewe
steps.stepSummary: Another version of the case: a ewe born to a goat, which was itself born to a ewe. רבי מאיר says the sheep-nature returned to its original place. חכמים say it did not return.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead that the case is a ewe born to a goat, which was itself born to a ewe. One master (רבי מאיר) holds that the sheep-nature came back to its place, so the newborn is obligated in בכורה. The other master (חכמים) holds that the sheep-nature did not come back, so it is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second possible case for the same dispute. Here the newborn looks like its grandmother but not like its direct mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the newborn sheep does not match its goat mother, but it does match its sheep grandmother. רבי מאיר sees this as the original sheep identity 'coming home', so it counts as matching. חכמים say only the direct mother counts, so this is a נדמה and is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: introduces an alternative answer
Sheep-nature: the quality of being a שה
Returned to their place: the original identity came back

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
with a ewe, daughter of a goat, daughter of a ewe,
phrases.notes: Three generations: sheep, then goat, then sheep (the newborn).

phrases.english: one master holds: the sheep-nature returned to its place,
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר: the newborn is obligated.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לֹא חָזְרוּ שֵׂיֻיוֹת לִמְקוֹמָן.
phrases.english: and the other master holds: the sheep-nature did not return to its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative case that reverses the order of the generations from step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a newborn that does not match its direct mother can never be obligated.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר holds that matching the grandmother restores the original identity, so the newborn is obligated.

steps.title: רב אשי: the newborn has only some of its mother's signs
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the ברייתא as a case where the newborn has some of its mother's signs. רבי מאיר obligates it, matching our משנה. The חכמים who disagree are רבי שמעון, who requires the head and most of the body to resemble the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: the case is where the newborn has some of its mother's signs. And who are the 'חכמים' who disagree? It is רבי שמעון, who says the newborn is not obligated unless its head and most of its body look like its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a completely different answer. He uses a single newborn that partly resembles its mother, instead of a multi-generation family tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, partial resemblance to the mother is enough, so the newborn counts as matching and the פסוק is satisfied. The 'חכמים' are identified as רבי שמעון, who demands that the head and majority of the body match. So the whole dispute is about how much resemblance is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Some of the signs: partial physical features of the mother
And who are the Sages? It identifies the anonymous opinion
Its head and the majority of its body

steps.whatToRemember: There are three explanations for how רבי מאיר obligates בכורה without contradicting 'אך בכור שור'. (1) A ewe born to a ewe born to a goat: follow the mother or the grandmother? (2) A ewe born to a goat born to a ewe: does the sheep-nature return? (3) רב אשי: partial signs are enough for רבי מאיר, while רבי שמעון requires the head and most of the body.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the ברייתא to the known dispute in our משנה about how much resemblance to the mother is needed for בכורה.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
for example, where it has some of the signs,
phrases.notes: Some of its mother's features. רבי מאיר obligates, like our משנה.

phrases.english: and who are the 'Sages'? Rabbi Shimon,
who says: not until its head and the majority of its body
resemble its mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, independent explanation of the ברייתא that replaces the generational cases with partial resemblance.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case and identifying the anonymous opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'חכמים' seemed to be the majority view, which would leave רבי מאיר contradicting the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case involves partial signs. The dispute is between רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון over how much resemblance is needed, and neither contradicts the פסוק.

steps.title: רבי מאיר agrees the goat of ראש חודש must come from a goat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits רבי מאיר: for the שעיר of ראש חודש, the goat must be born from a goat, based on the word ״אחד״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי מאיר agrees that for the goat of ראש חודש we need the son of a female goat. What is the reason? The verse says ״אחד״, one. This means a goat that is special to its own kind, the way it has been since the six days of creation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a limit to רבי מאיר's view. Even though רבי מאיר is lenient about a נדמה in other places, he agrees that the ראש חודש goat must be a real goat, born from a goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier steps, רבי מאיר treated an animal born of mixed-looking parentage as fine, for example by saying the sheep-nature 'returned.' Here רבי יוחנן says that for this special קרבן, the extra word ״אחד״ requires a pure goat. That means a goat born from a goat, unchanged since creation.

keyTerms.meaning: The male goat brought as a חטאת on ראש חודש
The son of a female goat
The one that is special or distinct to its own kind
The six days of creation, meaning the original natural species

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי מאיר's leniency about a נדמה has limits. For certain קרבנות, the Torah demands species purity.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּשָׂעִיר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir concedes regarding the goat of the New Moon
that we require the son of a female goat.
What is the reason? The verse states:
"One", meaning the one that is distinct,
as it has come from the six days of Creation.
phrases.notes: The species must be unchanged from how it was created.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limitation to רבי מאיר's lenient view as explained in the earlier answers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to רבי מאיר, the שעיר of ראש חודש must be born from a goat, because of the word ״אחד״.

steps.title: Isn't this already learned from a different verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a נדמה is already excluded from קרבנות by ״שור או כשב או עז״, so why do we need ״אחד״?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is this learned from here? It is learned from there! ״שור או כשב״ excludes כלאים, a mixed breed. ״או עז״ excludes a נדמה, an animal that looks like another species.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's source. It points out that a different verse already teaches that a look-alike animal cannot be a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ויקרא, ״שור או כשב או עז כי יולד״, already disqualifies both a mixed breed and a נדמה. If so, the word ״אחד״ in the ראש חודש verse seems unnecessary. The attack is about a repeated, extra source.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned from here
It is learned from there, a different source
To exclude a mixed breed from two species
To exclude an animal that looks like a different species

phrases.english: But is it derived from here?
It is derived from there:
"A bull or a sheep" excludes a mixed breed;
"or a goat" excludes a look-alike.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source רבי יוחנן used.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of ״אחד״ as the source for requiring species purity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different verse already excludes a נדמה, so ״אחד״ seems to repeat something we already know.

steps.title: Both verses are needed
steps.stepSummary: Each verse teaches something the other could not. ״או עז״ alone might not cover a look-alike that resembles its ancestors. ״אחד״ alone might only apply to obligatory קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If we only had the verse from there, I would say: that only applies when the look-alike does not trace back to earlier generations. But when it does trace back, I would say it is not excluded. And if we only had the verse from here, I would say: that only applies to an obligatory קרבן, but a voluntary one, no. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a צריכא. It explains why each verse is necessary and cannot be learned from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״או עז״ alone would only exclude an animal that looks like nothing in its family. It would not exclude one whose look goes back to a grandparent, like the case in the earlier steps. ״אחד״ covers that case, but it appears in a חובה offering, so it alone might not apply to a נדבה. Together they disqualify both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary, meaning both sources are needed
Traces back to earlier generations
An obligatory קרבן
A voluntary gift offering

steps.confusionAlert: ״מהתם״ here means the verse in ויקרא (״שור או כשב או עז״), and ״מהכא״ means the ראש חודש verse (״אחד״). Don't mix them up.
steps.whatToRemember: Two verses work together. ״או עז״ teaches the general rule against a נדמה. ״אחד״ extends it to a look-alike that traces back to an ancestor.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for if it were from there alone, I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא נְחַת לְדָרֵי,
phrases.english: this applies only where it does not trace back to earlier generations,
but where it does trace back, I would say no.
And if it were from here alone, I would have said:
this applies only to an obligatory offering,
but a gift offering, no. So both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by showing that each verse is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source teaches something unique
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One verse alone would leave out either a look-alike that traces back to an ancestor or a voluntary offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both verses are needed to disqualify every kind of נדמה from every קרבן.

steps.title: No מלקות for שעטנז with wool from a changed animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר יעקב: everyone agrees there is no מלקות for כלאים when the wool comes from a נדמה, because wool must be unchanged, like linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר יעקב said: Everyone agrees that we do not give מלקות for its wool because of כלאים. The verse says ״לא תלבש שעטנז״. Just as linen has not changed, so too the wool must be from an animal that has not changed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new statement about a נדמה in a different area, the laws of שעטנז. The wool of a changed-looking animal does not bring מלקות when it is mixed with linen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse puts wool next to linen. Linen is a plant that never changes from its kind, so the wool must also come from an animal that has not changed from its parents. Even רבי מאיר agrees to this, which is why it says 'everyone agrees.'

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
We give מלקות, lashes
A forbidden mix of wool and linen
Has changed

phrases.english: Rabbi Aḥa bar Yaakov said:
Everyone agrees that one is not flogged
for its wool because of diverse kinds,
as it says: "You shall not wear שעטנז".
Just as linen has not changed,
so too, wool that has not changed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement in the series about a נדמה, now applied to כלאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no מלקות for wearing linen mixed with wool from a נדמה, since the wool must be unchanged like linen.

steps.title: Wool of a look-alike animal cannot be used for blue fringes
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא: everyone agrees that wool from a נדמה is unfit for תכלת. The verse puts wool next to linen, so the wool must be unchanged like linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Everyone agrees that its wool is unfit for תכלת. The verse says 'Do not wear שעטנז… make yourself גדילים.' Just as linen is unchanged, so too the wool must be unchanged.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a second rule in the same style as רבי אחא בר יעקב. Wool from a look-alike animal cannot be used for the blue strings of ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about ציצית comes right after the verse that mentions wool and linen together. Linen is a plant that never 'changes species.' So the wool used for ציצית must also come from an animal that did not change.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees (even רבי מאיר, who obligates בכורה in the disputed look-alike cases)
The blue-dyed wool strings of ציצית
A forbidden mixture of wool and linen
Twisted cords, meaning ציצית

steps.confusionAlert: 'Everyone agrees' does not mean everyone agrees about בכורה. Even רבי מאיר, who obligates בכורה in the disputed look-alike cases of the ברייתא, agrees that the wool of such an animal is unfit here.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Everyone agrees that its wool is unfit for sky-blue fringes,
as it says: 'Do not wear diverse kinds…'
'you shall make yourself twisted cords,'
just as linen is something that has not changed,
so too only wool that has not changed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי אחא בר יעקב's 'unchanged like linen' derivation to תכלת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wool of a נדמה is unfit for תכלת, according to all opinions.

steps.title: Wool of a look-alike animal cannot become impure with צרעת marks
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק: everyone agrees that a garment made of a נדמה's wool cannot become impure through נגעים. The verse pairs wool with linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Everyone agrees that its wool does not become impure with נגעים. The verse says 'a wool garment or a linen garment.' Just as linen is unchanged, so too the wool must be unchanged.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third rule in the same pattern. Wool from a look-alike animal does not become impure through צרעת marks on clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about garment צרעת mentions wool and linen side by side. Linen never changes species, so the wool must also come from an animal that did not change. This time the rule makes things more lenient, because the wool cannot become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: צרעת marks that can make a garment impure
Becomes ritually impure
Linen

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים שֶׁאֵין צַמְרוֹ מִטַּמֵּא בִּנְגָעִים,
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that its wool does not become impure with leprous marks,
as it says: 'in a wool garment or in a linen garment,'
just as linen has not changed,
so too only wool that has not changed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel application of the same derivation, this time to נגעים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wool of a נדמה does not become impure with נגעים.

steps.title: Wine from a vine trellised over a fig tree is unfit for libations
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי extends the pattern to plants. Wine from a vine trellised over a fig tree is 'changed,' so it is unfit for נסכים, just as a קרבן must be unchanged.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We too can say that if someone trellised a vine over a fig tree, its wine is unfit for נסכים. Why? The verse says 'זבח and נסכים.' Just as the זבח must be unchanged, so too the נסכים must be unchanged.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes the 'must be unchanged' idea and applies it to a new area, wine poured on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal קרבן cannot be a נדמה, as we learned earlier from 'שור או כשב או עז.' The verse places נסכים next to זבח, so the wine must also come from an unchanged source. A vine growing over a fig tree is treated as changed.

keyTerms.meaning: Trellised, meaning trained a vine to grow over something
Wine libations poured on the מזבח
An animal offering
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַף אָנוּ נֹאמַר,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: We too can say,
if one trellised a grapevine over a fig tree,
its wine is unfit for libations.
What is the reason? 'An offering and libations':
just as the offering must be one that has not changed,
so too the libations must be ones that have not changed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַף אָנוּ נֹאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the 'unchanged' principle from animals to plants
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine from a vine trellised over a fig tree is unfit for נסכים.

steps.title: If trellising changes a plant, linen would be 'changed' too
steps.stepSummary: רבינא objects to רב אשי. If trellising counts as a change, then flax trellised over a shrub is changed too. Then the earlier derivations, which rely on 'linen never changes,' would fall apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged: If someone trellised flax over a shrub, is it also changed? If so, you can no longer say 'just as linen is unchanged,' because linen can change too!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רב אשי's new rule. He shows that it would break the earlier rules that are built on linen being unchanged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every derivation above depends on linen being the model of something that never changes. If growing one plant over another counts as a change, flax can change as well. Then linen can no longer serve as the 'unchanged' model.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it
A type of thorny shrub
If so

phrases.english: Ravina challenged it:
If one trellised flax over a shrub,
would it also be considered changed?
If so, you cannot say
'just as linen has not changed,'
since linen also can change!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's extension
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule that trellising makes a plant 'changed'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If trellising counts as a change, linen can also be changed. That would undermine every derivation that uses linen as the model of an unchanged material.

steps.title: Only a change in scent counts
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that a vine growing over a fig tree changes its scent. Flax growing over a shrub does not change its scent, so the flax is not considered changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: This one, the wine, has a changed scent. That one, the flax, does not have a changed scent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא. He sets a standard for what counts as a change: a change in scent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every trellising counts as a change. A change only matters when it is noticeable, as when the wine picks up a fig smell. Flax keeps its character, so linen is still a valid 'unchanged' model and both rulings stand.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him
Its scent
Has changed

steps.whatToRemember: The rule is 'just as linen is unchanged, so too the wool must be unchanged.' On this basis, a נדמה's wool is excluded from כלאים, תכלת, and נגעים. Wine from a vine trellised over a fig tree is unfit for נסכים because its scent changes. Flax is not affected, because its scent stays the same.

phrases.english: He said to him:
This one, the wine, has changed its scent,
and that one, the flax, has not changed its scent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any trellising, whether of a vine or of flax, would count as a change.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a change that alters the scent counts. The vine's scent changes and the flax's does not.

steps.title: Twin males born together: both go to the priest
steps.stepSummary: The משנה presents a ewe whose first birth is two males, with both heads emerging at once. רבי יוסי הגלילי rules that both go to the כהן, based on the plural word הזכרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A ewe that had never given birth before had two male lambs, and both of their heads came out at the same time. רבי יוסי הגלילי says: both of them go to the כהן, because the verse says 'the males (plural) are for ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a twin-birth case. The first opinion, רבי יוסי הגלילי, says both lambs are בכורות and both go to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only the first animal to leave the womb is a בכור. Here both seem to come out together, so רבי יוסי הגלילי accepts that two animals can share the 'first' status. He supports this from the plural word הַזְּכָרִים, which shows the Torah can treat more than one male as a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. Marks the start of a new משנה.
A ewe (female sheep)
That has not yet given birth for the first time
At the same moment
'The males are for ה׳‎' (שמות יג:יב). The plural is the basis for the ruling

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the משנה: can two births happen at exactly the same instant? Everything else in the משנה depends on that question.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
phrases.notes: Opening marker of a new משנה

phrases.english: A ewe that had not yet given birth
and it gave birth to two males
and both of their heads came out as one
phrases.notes: For animals, the head coming out counts as the birth

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says
both of them go to the priest
as it is stated: "The males shall be to the Lord"
phrases.notes: The plural 'males' allows more than one בכור

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רָחֵל שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרָה וְיָלְדָה שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It moves away from the discussion of a נדמה that ran from step 8 through step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, when two male firstborn lambs emerge simultaneously, both are בכורות and both are given to the כהן.

steps.title: The חכמים: exact simultaneity is impossible, so the twins are split
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue that two births can never happen at precisely the same moment. So only one lamb is truly the בכור, but we do not know which one. Therefore one goes to the owner and one to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: it is impossible for two things to happen at exactly the same instant. So one lamb went first, and only it is the בכור. Since we do not know which, one lamb stays with the owner and one goes to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with רבי יוסי הגלילי. They say one lamb must have come out first, so only one goes to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is not about the verse but about reality. The חכמים hold that 'at the same time' is never perfectly exact, so there is exactly one בכור. Since we cannot tell which lamb it is, each lamb is a ספק בכור. The fair outcome is to give one to each side.

keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible to be exact. Two events never line up perfectly in time
One for him, meaning the owner

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are NOT saying that neither lamb is a בכור. They are saying exactly one IS a בכור, and we simply do not know which one.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of אי אפשר לצמצם appears in many places in ש״ס. This is one of its classic sources.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say
it is impossible to be precise
phrases.notes: One birth must have come slightly before the other

phrases.english: rather, one is for him and one is for the priest

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי יוסי הגלילי from step 27 by denying that a truly simultaneous birth is possible.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two births cannot be exactly simultaneous, so only one lamb is a בכור. One lamb goes to the owner and one goes to the כהן.

steps.title: רבי טרפון: the priest picks the nicer lamb
steps.stepSummary: Working within the חכמים' view that the lambs are split, רבי טרפון says the כהן may choose the better of the two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: the כהן chooses the nicer of the two lambs for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the משנה asks a follow-up question: once we split the lambs, which one does the כהן get? רבי טרפון says the כהן gets to pick the better one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The split from step 28 leaves open which lamb the כהן receives. רבי טרפון lets the כהן choose. This means the owner bears the loss of the uncertainty.

keyTerms.meaning: Chooses or selects
The nicer or better one

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon says
the priest chooses for himself the better one

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּהֵן בּוֹרֵר לוֹ אֶת הַיָּפֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the חכמים' split in step 28 and asks which lamb the כהן receives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the twins are split, the כהן picks the better lamb.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: assess the lambs, and the owner's lamb grazes until blemished
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי טרפון. The lambs are assessed between the parties, and the כהן takes the leaner one. The lamb that stays with the owner must graze until it gets a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: we assess the lambs between them, and the כהן ends up with the leaner one. The second lamb, which stays with the owner, must be left to graze until it gets a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a different method for dividing the lambs, which the גמרא will explain. The משנה then says what the owner does with the lamb he keeps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not let the כהן simply take the better lamb. The lambs are assessed, and the כהן receives the leaner one, because one who wants to take from another must bring proof. The owner's lamb might be the real בכור, so he cannot eat it while it is unblemished. It must graze until it gets a מום, and then he may slaughter and eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: They assess the fatness or value between them. The כהן receives the leaner lamb
It must graze, meaning it is left to pasture
Until it becomes blemished (gets a מום)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views. רבי יוסי הגלילי: both lambs go to the כהן. חכמים: אי אפשר לצמצם, so the lambs are split. Within the split, רבי טרפון says the כהן picks the better one, and רבי עקיבא says the כהן gets the leaner one. The owner's lamb is a ספק בכור and must graze until it gets a מום.
steps.confusionAlert: 'The second' lamb is not a definite חולין animal. It might be the real בכור, which is exactly why the owner cannot eat it until it is blemished.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says
they assess the lambs between them
phrases.notes: The גמרא explains this: the כהן takes the leaner lamb

phrases.english: and the second must graze until it becomes blemished
phrases.notes: The lamb kept by the owner is a ספק בכור

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי טרפון in step 29 about how the split works, then rules on the status of the owner's lamb.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lambs are assessed and the כהן gets the leaner one. The owner's lamb is a ספק בכור and must graze until it gets a מום.
